messages.content: We’re ready to compare San Diego dates. It would be the three of us from O’Hare. The two options are Saturday, July 18 through Saturday, July 25, or Saturday, July 25 through Sunday, August 2. Which window looks more workable overall?

I’ll compare them as a seven-night trip versus an eight-night trip, looking at nonstop flight schedules, current economy fares, and lodging supply for three guests. I’ll also check whether any major events are distorting one part of the calendar.
Right. We haven’t decided how much of the total budget should go to flights versus the hotel, so I’m more interested in the shape of the options than the absolute cheapest package.

The flight schedules are workable in both windows. Each has morning and midday nonstop choices from ORD to SAN, with nonstop returns ranging from late morning into the evening. The first window currently prices around $1,260 to $1,470 total for three in standard economy. The second is roughly $1,350 to $1,590, depending on the return time.
So the second week costs a little more in the air. Is there any schedule advantage that makes up for it?

A modest one. On July 25, there are two nonstop departures that reach San Diego before noon without requiring a very early start. On July 18, the lower fares are concentrated on the earliest departure or an afternoon arrival. Returning August 2 also has more nonstop choices after 2:00 p.m. than the July 25 return.
An extra night is useful, but not if the hotel market is much worse. What are you seeing there?

The lodging comparison favors July 25 to August 2, despite a tight first night. A large convention affects central San Diego late in the first window. For July 18 to 25, many downtown properties either have limited room types or sharply higher rates for the final few nights. Some seven-night totals are being pushed above $3,300 before parking and resort charges.

Saturday, July 25 is still constrained, but availability opens considerably from July 26 onward. Across the full eight nights, there are more continuous stays in the broader central and coastal areas, generally around $2,700 to $3,500 before property-specific fees. There are also more room configurations that plausibly accommodate two adults and a 12-year-old without changing rooms mid-stay.
Could we avoid the expensive first night by flying Sunday the 26th and still come back August 2?

Yes, but that reduces the trip to seven nights. Sunday airfare is currently about $120 to $210 more for all three than the better Saturday combinations. The hotel savings could exceed that, though: arriving July 26 removes the most constrained night and brings several full-stay lodging options down by roughly $250 to $450.
I’d rather preserve the eight nights for now. Between the two original windows, which one would you carry forward?

July 25 to August 2 is the stronger working window. Airfare is somewhat higher, but the schedules are more flexible, the trip gains a night, and lodging supply improves after the first evening. The July 18 to 25 window runs directly into the convention-driven compression at the end, when moving dates or changing room types would be harder.
Use July 25 through August 2, then. Don’t book anything yet. Next I want to compare neighborhoods and actual room setups, including the full fees, rather than just nightly rates.

I’ll carry forward July 25 through August 2 for three travelers, with no reservations made. The next comparison will focus on neighborhood tradeoffs, rooms that genuinely fit all three guests, and complete stay totals including mandatory property charges.
